extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) interacting with the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements governing USPTO actions (statutory invention registrations, allowance/issuance, disclaimers, corrections, maintenance fees, and related petitions/notifications) for patent applicants, patentees, and their representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of request for statutory invention registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for publication of a statutory invention registration must include: (1) a waiver of the applicant’s right to receive a patent effective upon publication; (2) the required fee (per § 1.17(n) or (o)); (3) a statement that, in the requester’s opinion, the application meets the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112; and (4) a statement that, in the requester’s opinion, the application complies with the formal requirements of this part for printing as a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must be signed by (i) the applicant and any assignee of record or (ii) an attorney or agent of record in the application. These elements are mandatory for a valid request filed prior to March 16, 2013 (per editor note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of waiver filed with statutory invention registration request
rubrics_metrics.description: A waiver filed with a request for a statutory invention registration is effective upon publication to waive the inventor’s right to receive a patent on the invention claimed in the registration for any application pending on, or filed after, the date of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A waiver does not affect rights of any other inventor even if subject matter is commonly owned. A waiver will not affect rights in a patent issued prior to publication unless a reissue application is filed seeking to enlarge claims. See also § 1.104(c)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination standards for requests to publish statutory invention registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will examine a request for a statutory invention registration to determine: (1) if the subject matter is appropriate for publication; (2) if requirements for publication are met; and (3) if the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112 and § 1.293 are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant will be notified of results. If requirements are not met, notification sets a period to comply to avoid abandonment; noncompliance with 35 U.S.C. 112 results in a rejection under 112. Reply periods are subject to extension under § 1.136. Failure to timely meet requirements results in final refusal; if 112 defects persist, the 112 rejection is made final. Approval results in notice of intent to publish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review procedures for final refusal to publish statutory invention registration
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester dissatisfied with a final refusal to publish for reasons other than compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112 may petition the Director (with fee per § 1.17(g)) within one month or other time set in the decision; a requester dissatisfied with a final 35 U.S.C. 112 rejection may appeal to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (now PTAB) under § 41.31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions should comply with § 1.181(b). The petition may request refund of the petition fee if refusal (other than for 112) resulted from PTO error. If a 112 rejection is reversed on appeal, the request for registration will be approved and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of request for publication of statutory invention registration
rubrics_metrics.description: A filed request for a statutory invention registration may be withdrawn prior to notice of intent to publish by filing a request to withdraw; a withdrawal request filed on or after the notice of intent to publish must be in the form of a petition accompanied by the fee in § 1.17(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request to withdraw may request refund of amounts paid in excess of the application filing fee, but a handling fee of $130.00 will be retained. Editor notes apply to requests filed prior to March 16, 2013.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of statutory invention registration
rubrics_metrics.description: If approved, the statutory invention registration will be published, mailed to the requester at the correspondence address (§ 1.33(a)), and a notice of publication will be published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each published registration will include a statement: 'A statutory invention registration is not a patent. It has the defensive attributes of a patent but does not have the enforceable attributes of a patent.' No article or advertisement may use the term 'patent' or suggestive terms when referring to a statutory invention registration. See 35 U.S.C. 157 for rights information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of allowance — issue and publication fee timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If examination shows applicant is entitled to a patent, a notice of allowance is sent specifying an issue fee and any required publication fee which must be paid within three months from mailing of the notice of allowance to avoid abandonment. The three-month period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization to charge a deposit account per § 1.18 may be filed only after mailing of the notice of allowance. Certain submissions after mailing (e.g., incorrect fee, fee transmittal form, or payment of issue fee) operate as a request to charge the deposit account identified in a previously filed authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may be made as a matter of right after mailing of the notice of allowance. Any amendment under this section must be filed before or with payment of the issue fee and may be entered on recommendation of the primary examiner and approval by the Director without withdrawing the application from issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after allowance are discretionary and subject to examiner/Director approval; procedural history cites multiple revisions and effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal from issue — petitions and Office-initiated withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be withdrawn from issue for further action upon petition by the applicant (with fee per § 1.17(h) and showing of good and sufficient reasons) or at the Office's initiative. A petition is not required if a request for continued examination (§ 1.114) is filed prior to payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Office withdraws application from issue and later allows it again, a new notice of allowance is issued. Once issue fee paid, Office will not withdraw on its own initiative except for: (1) Office mistake; (2) violation of § 1.56 or illegality; (3) unpatentability of one or more claims; or (4) interference or derivation proceeding. Applicant petitions after payment are limited to specific reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of patent and request to defer issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant timely pays the issue fee, the Office will issue the patent in regular course unless the application is withdrawn from issue or the Office defers issuance. To request deferral, applicant must file a petition with the fee in § 1.17(h) and a showing of good and sufficient reasons why deferral is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition to defer must be received and granted before the date of issue to be effective; withdrawal after payment of issue fee may not avoid publication of application information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for failure to pay issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If the issue fee is not paid within three months from the date of the notice of allowance, the application will be regarded as abandoned and will not be considered pending before the Patent and Trademark Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This three-month non-extendable period is strict; historical revisions noted in citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory disclaimers and terminal disclaimers requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee or applicant may disclaim any complete claim(s) or dedicate to the public the entire term or any terminal part of the term. A disclaimer/terminal disclaimer to be recorded must be signed, identify the patent and claim(s) or term being disclaimed, state the present extent of ownership interest, and be accompanied by the fee in § 1.20(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A terminal disclaimer filed to obviate judicially created double patenting must: comply with signature, specification of portion disclaimed, statement of ownership interest, fee, and include provisions waiving separate enforcement and that the patent will be enforceable only during periods when commonly owned with the application/patent forming the basis for double patenting. Special rules apply for double patenting arising from activities under joint research agreements (see paragraph d). Editor notes indicate different applicability for pre- and post-September 16, 2012 filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of correction for Office mistake (35 U.S.C. 254)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may issue a certificate of correction to correct a mistake in a patent incurred through the fault of the Office that is clearly disclosed in the records of the Office: at the request of the patentee/assignee, sua sponte, or on information from a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no obligation for the Office to act on third-party submissions; third-party papers will not be made of record or retained. If the patent is involved in an interference or PTAB trial, requests must comply with specified motion requirements (§ 41.121 or § 42.20). The Office will notify the patentee and afford an opportunity to be heard before issuing the certificate; if correction in this form is inappropriate, a corrected patent may be issued instead without expense to the patentee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of correction for applicant's mistake (35 U.S.C. 255)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may issue a certificate of correction under the conditions specified in 35 U.S.C. 255 at the request of the patentee or assignee, upon payment of the fee in § 1.20(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request relates to a patent involved in interference or PTAB trial, it must comply with motion requirements under § 41.121 or § 42.20. Historical citations reflect revisions and effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 256
rubrics_metrics.description: When through error an incorrect inventor is named or an actual inventor is omitted, the Director may issue a certificate naming only the actual inventor(s) on application of all parties and assignees or on a court order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be accompanied by: (1) a statement from each person being added and each currently named inventor agreeing to the change or stating no disagreement; (2) a statement from all assignees agreeing to the change that complies with § 3.73(c); and (3) the fee in § 1.20(b). For correction in an application see § 1.48. In interferences/contested cases, correction must be in form of a motion under the applicable PTAB rules (§ 41.121(a)(2) or § 42.22) and must comply with this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other mistakes not correctable after patent issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Mistakes other than those provided for in §§ 1.322, 1.323, 1.324, and not affording legal grounds for reissue or reexamination, will not be corrected after the date of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits post-issuance corrective mechanisms to specified statutory remedies (Office correction, applicant correction, inventorship correction) or reissue/reexamination where legally permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing notice of arbitration awards (35 U.S.C. 294)
rubrics_metrics.description: Written notice of any arbitrator award under 35 U.S.C. 294 must be filed in the Patent and Trademark Office by the patentee or the patentee’s assignee or licensee; if award involves more than one patent, a separate notice must be filed for each patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must list patent number, inventor and patent owner names, names and addresses of parties to arbitration, and include a copy of the award. If court modifies the award, the party requesting modification must file a notice of the modification with a copy of the court’s order. Any award is unenforceable until required notices are filed; if the designated party fails to file, any party to the arbitration may file the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees — applicability, timing windows, and effects of nonpayment
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees per §§ 1.20(e)–(g) are required to maintain patents in force beyond 4, 8, and 12 years after grant for patents based on applications filed on or after Dec 12, 1980, except plant and design patents. Maintenance fees may be paid without surcharge during specified windows: (1) 3 years through 3 years 6 months after grant (first fee); (2) 7 years through 7 years 6 months (second fee); (3) 11 years through 11 years 6 months (third fee). With surcharge, payment permitted during respective grace periods through the anniversary (4th, 8th, 12th).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a payment deadline falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday, payment may be made on the next non-holiday. Failure to pay maintenance fee and any surcharge within the prescribed periods causes the patent to expire at end of the grace period (expiration on anniversary date of grant). Periods for reissue applications are counted from grant date of the original non-reissue application. Historical and revision citations apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee address for maintenance fee notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices, receipts, refunds, and other communications relating to maintenance fee payment or refund are directed to the correspondence address used during prosecution (§ 1.33(a)) unless a fee address is set at time of submitting the issue fee, a change in correspondence address is filed after payment of the issue fee, or a fee address/change is filed after payment; the latest such address will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An assignment does not change correspondence or fee address for maintenance fee purposes. A fee address must be an address associated with a Customer Number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of maintenance fees — who may pay and acceptable methods
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee, or any person/organization on behalf of a patentee, may pay maintenance fees and any necessary surcharges. Payments must be the full amount due on the date paid and may be made using methods in § 1.23 or by authorization to charge a deposit account under § 1.25. Any payment or authorization must be submitted within the permitted periods (§ 1.362(d),(e),(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizations to charge a deposit account must authorize immediate charging. Payments filed at other times are not accepted except insofar as a delayed payment is accepted by the Director in an expired patent via petition under § 1.378. Payments in incorrect amount, by improper method, or authorizations with insufficient funds do not constitute payment. Procedures in §§ 1.8 or 1.10 may be utilized for paying maintenance fees and surcharges.
